title: The orchestrator signals completion; the branch remains the truth
description:
When the orchestrator finishes, the Workflow should learn it without polling. Containers can make outbound requests, so: orchestrator finishes -> POSTs a Worker endpoint -> the Worker calls instance.sendEvent(). A container invoking a Workflow binding DIRECTLY is unverified, so route through a Worker.

Verified semantics that shape this:
- Events are BUFFERED: 'You can send an event to a Workflow instance before it reaches the corresponding waitForEvent call.' A container that finishes before the Workflow resumes does not lose its completion, so the timing race is closed by the platform.
- Payload cap is 1 MiB. Send the branch and the head sha, never the work product.
- The event type must match ^[a-zA-Z0-9_][a-zA-Z0-9-_]*$ - no dots.

The caveat that decides the design: buffering closes the timing race but NOT the case where the container dies after finishing and before its callback lands. So the event is an optimisation and the pushed branch is the source of truth. A supervisor that trusted the event alone would report a finished run as failed.

That is the same rule the local reconciler already lives by - never take a claim's word for its own progress, read the durable evidence.
acceptance_criteria: A finished orchestrator wakes its Workflow without polling, and a run whose callback never lands is still concluded correctly from the branch
